waveName: Wave 4 – Cut placement & accents, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detection

package.title: PDF sheet structure: no paper-wasting strips, cut templates traceable from every sheet, code plans for tiny stones
package.goal: Sheets are split evenly with no thin strips, and the page count is predictable through a shared planner. Every cut piece on a sheet points to its template T#. Sheets whose stones are too small for 1:1 codes get matching code-plan pages.
steps: pdfOptions.ts: move the sheet reserves (M 10, top 19, left 12, bottom 21) into exported SHEET_RESERVES and printableArea(opts). Add codePlan: 'auto' | 'always' | 'off' (default 'auto').

pdfPlan.ts:
- balancedSplit(pos, size, a, b, maxLen): greedy count, then cut lines spread evenly on grid lines.
- planSheets(layout, sections, opts) → exact cell ranges per sheet.
- planPdfPages(layout, sections, opts, piecesPerSection, templateGroups?) → {total, front, sectionCovers, sheets, cutLists, codePlans, templates, coords}. It uses the same constants and the rows-per-page rules of the generator.
generatePdf uses planSheets.
Sections that fit on one sheet get a compact 'Abschnittsübersicht' block instead of a full cover, packed several per page. Multi-sheet sections keep their cover.

T# on sheets:
- For each cut piece, look up the T# from tpl.bySig (signature from pieceCutInfo).
- Print it as a small second line when it fits (about 4.5 mm on paper).
- Otherwise draw a doc.circle callout with a plain number.
- After each sheet with cut or uncoded pieces, add a 'Zuschnittliste Blatt A1-n' page (pure sheetCutList, exported) with the columns: No, ID, code, shape, T# or 'T512 (nicht im PDF)', outer size.
- Template boxes list occurrences per sheet instead of 12 IDs.
- Apply the same '(nicht im PDF)' rule in the coordinate list.

Code plan:
- Export labelOk(piece, s), used by the sheet drawing code.
- When a 1:1 sheet has unlabelled stones and codePlan allows it, add code pages right after it. They cover exactly the same cell range at k = the smallest integer ≥ 2 such that every stone passes labelOk.
- Title: 'Codeplan zu Blatt A1-1 (Teil i/n) – NICHT maßstäblich (k:1)'.
- No crosses, no 'deckungsgleich' hint and no 'Kontrollstrecke', but a clear marker text.
- Draw thin guide lines every 10 cells on both the sheet and the code pages.
acceptance: planPdfPages(...).total equals doc.getNumberOfPages() for the 4 samples, on A4 and A3, with coordinates and templates on and off.
No sheet is narrower than 40 % of the printable width unless its section is.

Every cut piece in the selected sections appears exactly once on its sheet's cut list or carries an on-piece T#, and its T# equals bySig.get(signature).no. No referenced T# exceeds templateLimit without '(nicht im PDF)'.

With 2 mm tiles at 1:1 and codePlan auto, the code pages contain exactly one code per piece and the per-colour code counts equal stats. The fills on the 1:1 sheets still equal stats (existing test; code pages excluded by their marker).
package.risk: Effort L. Section IDs and sheet numbering must stay stable for a given layout. Keep the 1:1 registration exactly as today.

findings.title: Sheet splitting wastes about half the paper: thin leftover strips, oversized margins, one full page per section cover
findings.problem: The default section size (300×300 mm) does not relate to the paper's printable area (A4 portrait 1:1: 178×247 mm). tilesOf() splits greedily (pdf.ts:433-446), so many sections become one full sheet plus a 16–40 mm strip on a separate page. Fixed reserves (M=10, top 19, bottom 21, pdf.ts:84/427-429) take 60 of 297 mm. Every section also gets a separate cover page that is mostly empty. The UI estimate (StepPdf.tsx:31-36: PH-53 and ceil(w/printW)) uses different numbers from pdf.ts (PH-50 and grid-aligned greedy split).
findings.evidence: sheets.py on the generated PDFs: a4p_12mm (60×40 cm, 12 mm) has 12 sheets, 6 of which are only 26–40 mm wide (png/a12-09.png). many_templates (400×500) has 9 sheets, 3 of them 16 mm high. en_a4_3mm has 175 mm + a 23 mm strip. waste.ts (exact replica of tilesOf): paper utilisation 45–51 % with defaults. 60×40 cm: 12 sheets, but 8 if sections equal the printable area. 200×100 cm: 98 sheets, 56 with tighter margins (M 7 / top 14 / bottom 12). 1000×500 cm: 2312 laying sheets vs 1197 (94 % utilisation) with page-sized sections. 500×250 cm PDF: 1134 pages, of which 153 are section covers (out/big_500x250.pdf).
findings.proposal: (1) Export the printable-area function from pdfOptions.ts (one source of truth for pdf.ts and StepPdf's estimate). Offer an 'Abschnitt = 1 Blatt (A4 1:1: 178 × 247 mm)' preset, or default the section size to whole multiples of the printable area / sheetScale. (2) In tilesOf, after the greedy count k, distribute columns/rows evenly (same idea as splitAxis in layout.ts) so there are no strips. Try both orientations per section and keep the one with fewer sheets (jsPDF addPage takes orientation per page; 1:1 accuracy is unaffected). (3) Reduce reserves: header 14 mm, footer 12 mm (hint and calibration bar on one line). (4) Put the section cover info on the first sheet's free area when it fits, or put 2 section covers per page.
corrected:
1) One source of truth for the printable area. Export from pdfOptions.ts a sheetGeometry(opts) that returns {M:10, left:12, top:19, bottom:21, printW, printH}, plus a pure sheetSplit(layout, section, scale, printW, printH) with the same logic as tilesOf. Use both in pdf.ts:427-446 and in StepPdf.tsx:29-36, so the estimate always equals the real sheet count. The estimate should also count the section cover pages.

2) Section size presets in StepPlan.tsx, next to the section-size inputs at ~line 130. Add buttons "1 Blatt" and "2×2 Blätter" that set sectionWmm/sectionHmm = k·printW/s × k·printH/s from the project's current pdfOptions (A4 portrait 1:1 gives 178×247 mm or 356×494 mm). Keep the 30×30 cm default, since it matches common mesh sheets and existing projects' section IDs and progress would shift. In StepPdf, show a hint when any section's last sheet column or row is narrower than 25 % of printW/printH. Name the strip size and the suggested preset in the hint.

3) Cover pages. When a section fits on a single sheet (nT===1), skip its separate cover. Instead write a compact "Abschnittsübersicht" block (id, X/Y, size, neighbours, stone count, per-colour code:count list) and pack several blocks per page. Multi-sheet sections keep their full cover. Measured page totals for 1000×500 cm: about 1197 sheets plus summary pages with the 1-sheet preset, or 1276+319 with the 2×2 preset, vs 2890 today.

4) Drop "both orientations per section": measured zero gain. Treat even redistribution in tilesOf as optional cosmetics, because it does not lower the sheet count. Smaller margins are low priority: they help only by coincidence and need a relayout of the T-9 column labels, the ruler, and the PH-M-9 side info line. 1:1 scale, grid-aligned sheet edges and the joining marks must stay unchanged; add a test that sheets × printable area ≥ section area and that the PDF page count equals the UI estimate.

**1. (S, do first) Balanced sheet split.**
- Export a balancedSplit(pos, size, a, b, maxLen) from layout.ts. It is the existing splitAxis logic, generalized to a sub-range.
- Use it in computeSections and in pdf.ts tilesOf, with maxLen = printW/s and printH/s.
- This removes every narrow strip (e.g. A1-2 at X 171-197 mm becomes two sheets of about 98 mm) without changing sheet count, section IDs or geometry.
- The mini sheet overview, join labels and registration crosses all come from cx/ry, so they stay consistent.
- Keep the PDF==preview per-colour count test and add one: for every section, no sheet is narrower than 40% of the printable width unless the section itself is.

**2. (M) One source of truth for the printable area.**
- Add printableArea(opts) and SHEET_RESERVES {M:10, top:19, left:12, bottom:21} to pdfOptions.ts.
- Use them in pdf.ts:427-431 and in StepPdf's estimate.
- Have StepPdf compute the estimate with the same grid-aligned split instead of ceil(w/printW).

**3. (M) Paper-aligned sections.**
- Add sectionMode 'sheets' with sheetsPerSection X/Y, default 2x2.
- Compute sheet boundaries for the whole project first:
  - Walk the real colX/colW and rowY/rowH greedily against printW/sheetScale and printH/sheetScale, so cut edge cells and different tile sizes are handled exactly.
  - Rebalance these boundaries over the whole project.
- Group k x k sheets into one section, so section edges always fall on sheet edges.
- In this mode tilesOf returns exactly those global boundaries.
- Expected results: 2000x1000 cm drops from 126 to about 90 pages, 10000x5000 from 2890 to about 1570, with no strips.
- Make it the default only for NEW projects.
- In the PDF step, show a hint when paper use is under about 70% or strips exist, for example: "Abschnitte passen schlecht zu A4: 12 Blätter, 6 davon schmal – Abschnitte an Papier anpassen (8 Blätter)".
- Ask for confirmation if laying progress exists or a PDF was already exported, because section IDs and earlier printouts change. Progress is per cell, so no data is lost.
- Recompute when the paper format, orientation or scale changes.

**4. Orientation.**
- Do NOT mix orientations inside one PDF: print dialogs may auto-rotate or shrink to fit and break 1:1.
- Instead, let the estimate compute portrait vs landscape for the whole document and show "Querformat: N Blätter".

**5. Margins.**
- Keep M=10 so the calibration bar and labels survive printer non-printable edges.
- Only optional and verified by rendering: shrink bottomReserve by putting the joint hint and the calibration bar on one row.
- Only shrink topReserve if the sheet title moves into the running header first, because column labels at T-9 (pdf.ts:604) otherwise collide with the title at M+3.5 (pdf.ts:551).

**6. Section covers.**
- With k x k sections the cover overhead is already about 20%.
- Optionally, when exporting all sections, let covers flow: start a new page only when the next cover block (key data + legend table) does not fit in the space left. When printing a single section, keep its own cover page so it can still be printed separately.

findings.title: Cut pieces on the laying sheets don't point to their cut template, and tiny pieces carry no colour code
findings.problem: drawSheet() prints only the 2-digit colour code on every piece (pdf.ts:579-598). Pieces whose bounding box is under 1.8 mm on paper get no label at all (pdf.ts:592). The only links from a piece to its template are (a) the template box, which lists at most 12 IDs (collectTemplates, pdf.ts:69), and (b) the coordinate list, which stops at coordLimit (default 20 000). So at the wall, the user sees a trapezoid or sliver on the sheet and cannot find out which template (T#) to cut it from. This is the central requirement-5/9 link between the laying plan and the cut templates.
findings.evidence: Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/pdf-print/orphan.ts (200x100 cm, 8 mm, default PDF options) prints: "cutPieces=1914 cut pieces without any template reference in the PDF=753" (39 %). persize.ts: on the template boxes alone, 50 % (2x1 m), 24 % (30x40 cm/5 mm) and 57 % (60x40 cm/12 mm) of cut-piece IDs are not listed. The text in the content streams of the laying-sheet pages 9/10/12/13 of out/a4p_5mm_1to1.pdf contains 0 strings of the form 'T<n>'. codes.py: page 9 has 1059 stones drawn but only about 1035 code labels, so the missing ones are the small cut slivers. Visual: png/a5hi-09-eye.png (eye area: slivers with no code, trapezoids with no T#).
findings.proposal: In drawSheet, for non-FULL cells get ci = pieceCutInfo(cache, …) (the cache and tpl = collectTemplates(...) already exist before the sheet loop, pdf.ts:421) and tg = tpl.bySig.get(ci.signature). If the piece's inscribed size on paper is at least 3.5 mm, print two lines: the code and a small 'T12'. If it is smaller, draw a numbered callout dot (①②…) at the centroid and add a 'Zuschnitte auf diesem Blatt' table in the sheet's bottom reserve (marker · ID · code · T# · outer size). Add printH reserve for it, or continue on a follow-up page labelled with the sheet ID. On each template, replace the 12-ID list with occurrences per sheet ('A1-1: 14×, A1-2: 3×') so every instance can be traced. Use the same signature mapping the coordinate list uses, so no new geometry is invented. Add a vitest check: every cut piece's T# appears either on its sheet or in that sheet's table.
corrected:
All changes go in src/core/pdf.ts (plus src/core/csv.ts and tests). Every T# comes from the existing tpl.bySig signature mapping, so no new geometry is computed.

1. Print T# on the sheet.
   - In drawSheet, for each non-FULL piece: ci = pieceCutInfo(cache, layout, data, row, col, i, p.poly, raw(p.color)).
   - If ci.needsCut, look up tg = tpl.bySig.get(ci.signature). tpl, cache and raw already exist before the sheet loop.
   - Mark the template as printed only if opts.includeTemplates is true and tg.no <= opts.templateLimit.
   - If min(bbox)*s is at least about 3.5 mm and a T# font of at least 3 pt fits, print the code plus a second small line: 'T12' if printed, otherwise a scissors-free marker such as '*'.

2. Callouts for small pieces.
   - Cover cut pieces that are too small for two lines, and every piece that currently gets no code (the line 592 rule).
   - Draw a small circle (doc.circle) at the centroid with a plain running number 1..n per sheet, in helvetica digits. Do not use Unicode circled digits.

3. Cut list page per sheet.
   - When a sheet has any cut pieces, add a 'Zuschnittliste Blatt A1-3' page right after it. Do not shrink printH or bottomReserve.
   - Use the existing table() helper with columns: No. | Position ID (cellId + -i) | colour code + swatch | T# (or 'Vorlage nicht gedruckt') | shape | outer size w x h mm.

4. Template boxes.
   - In collectTemplates, also count occurrences per sheet.
   - Print 'A1-1: 14x, A1-2: 3x ...' instead of the first 12 IDs.

5. CSV.
   - In csv.ts, write the Zuschnitt column as 'ja (T12)', using the same collectTemplates numbering.

6. Vitest.
   - For a sample project, check that every cut piece on each generated sheet has either an on-piece T# or a cut-list row.
   - Check that no referenced T# is greater than templateLimit.
   - Check that every piece is labelled with its colour code either on the sheet or in the list.

src/core/pdf.ts:
(1) Add a pure exported function sheetCutList(layout, data, palette, materials, tpl, cache, r0, r1, c0, c1, s, showCodes). It returns one entry {id, code, shape, tNo|null, w, h} for every needsCut piece and for every piece whose code label was suppressed. Sort by row, then column. It reuses pieceCutInfo, tpl.bySig and pieceId, so no new geometry. In drawSheet, when the list is non-empty, print it on a follow-up page titled 'Zuschnittliste Blatt A1-3' (same header, page numbering included), in 4-5 compact columns of about 4 mm rows: 'C014-2 · 07 · Trapez · T12 · 7,9×4,1'. Continue on more pages labelled with the same sheet ID; at most about 200 entries per A4 page. This list is not subject to coordLimit.
(2) On the sheet, print the T# as a small second line inside the piece only when 4*area/perimeter*s >= ~4.5 mm (helps at 8-12 mm tiles or 2:1). No callout dots.
(3) Mark each piece whose code is suppressed with a tiny hollow dot (meaning 'see the cut list'), so slivers are never silently unlabelled. Only computed codes are shown.
(4) Never print a bare T# for a template that is not in the PDF. Keep global numbering so separately printed sections stay consistent. When opts.sectionIds is set, always print the templates referenced by the selected sections. If includeTemplates is false or tNo > templateLimit, print 'T512 (nicht im PDF)'. Apply the same rule to the coordinate list at pdf.ts:842.
(5) In drawTemplate, replace the 12-ID list with occurrences per sheet ('A1-3: 14×, A2-1: 3×' ...), built in collectTemplates by also recording the sheet. Truncate with '…' when the box is full.
(6) Vitest in tests/pdf.test.ts: for 2-3 sample projects, every cut piece in the selected sections appears exactly once, in sheetCutList for the sheet containing its cell. Its tNo equals tpl.bySig.get(signature).no. The sum of cut entries equals computeStats(...).cutPieces for those sections. The test also checks the i18n keys in de/en/tr. If showCodes is false for a whole sheet (e.g. 2 mm tiles at 1:1), print a warning on the sheet to choose scale >= 2:1 instead of listing every stone.

findings.title: At 1:1, stones under 2.2 mm get no colour codes at all, so the user must choose between true size and codes
findings.problem: showCodes = minCell >= 2.2 (pdf.ts:565). With 2 mm stones (a supported size) the 1:1 sheets are only coloured squares. Printed colours cannot tell 16–64 palette shades apart. The UI only shows a warning ('2:1 oder größer wählen'). That gives up the 1:1 laying sheet, which is the point of the 1:1 scale (direct method), and still gives no code reference for the 1:1 print.
findings.evidence: codes.py on out/a4p_2mm_1to1.pdf page 6: 'stones drawn (B ops)=3600, two-digit code labels=2'; the two are ruler labels, so no stone is coded. Visual png/a2-06.png. The 2:1 variant (out/a4p_2mm_2to1.pdf) has codes, but its sheets are not true size (4 sheets instead of 1).
findings.proposal: Add a sheet mode '1:1 + Codeplan', the default when tile*scale < 2.2 mm. After each 1:1 sheet, emit companion code sheet(s) for exactly the same cell range at the smallest scale k ∈ {2,3,4} with min(tileW,tileH)*k ≥ 2.5 mm. Title them 'Codeplan zu Blatt A1-1 – NICHT maßstäblich (k:1)', with the same row/column labels and IDs, and without registration crosses or the 'deckungsgleich' hint. On the 1:1 sheet, print the row letter/column number grid every 5 cells inside the joints so the user can find the matching cell on the code sheet. Update the UI warning to describe this.
corrected:
1) src/core/pdf.ts: work out which stones on each 1:1 sheet would have no code. Turn the code-label test (pdf.ts:565 and :592) into a small helper `labelOk(cellOrPiece, s)` that both the drawing code and this check use. If at least one stone on a 1:1 sheet has no code, and the user chose the new option `codePlan: 'auto' | 'always' | 'off'` (default 'auto' in src/core/pdfOptions.ts), add code sheets for that sheet directly after it.

2) How to build the code sheets:
- Use k = the smallest of {2, 3, 4} where every stone on the sheet passes `labelOk(·, k)`. That means k·min(tileW,tileH) ≥ 2.2 and k·min(piece bbox) ≥ 1.8 for every cut piece in that range.
- Cover exactly the cell range [c0,c1)×[r0,r1) of the 1:1 sheet. Split it with the existing `split()` logic from `tilesOf`, generalised from a whole section to an arbitrary cell range.
- Draw them with a variant of `drawSheet` (for example a `mode: 'codes'` parameter) that keeps the row and column labels and the absolute-mm ruler, and draws stones as white or lightly tinted outlines with large codes. This uses less ink and is easier to read.
- Leave out registration crosses and alignment marks, the 'deckungsgleich' hint and the 'Kontrollstrecke' box.
- Title: 'Codeplan zu Blatt A1-1 (Teil i/n) – NICHT maßstäblich (k:1) – nur zum Nachschlagen der Farbnummern'.
- Optionally, on the 1:1 sheet, draw thin guide lines every 10 cells along the joint centrelines so a cell is easier to find in the middle of a sheet. Do not put text inside the joints; the margin labels already exist.

3) Tests: tests/pdf.test.ts counts stone fills on streams that contain 'Blatt' and 'Kontrollstrecke'. Code sheets must not contain 'Kontrollstrecke' and must carry a clear marker. Add a test for 2 mm tiles at 1:1 with codePlan 'auto' that checks two things: every stone ID or position on the 1:1 sheets appears with its code on exactly one code sheet, and the fill totals on the 1:1 sheets still match computeStats.

4) src/ui/project/StepPdf.tsx:
- Compute the real scale per section, including fit mode, where s = min(printW/sec.w, printH/sec.h) instead of `opts.sheetScale || 1`.
- Use the same `labelOk` test (or counts from the worker) to show how many stones would have no code, for example '13.400 Steine ohne Farbnummer bei 1:1 → Codeplan-Seiten (2:1) werden angehängt, +N Seiten'.
- Add an option for the code plan: automatic / always / off.
- Update the warning text and add the new strings in src/i18n/de.ts, en.ts and tr.ts.
- Show the extra page count in the page estimate (StepPdf.tsx:34-35), because at k=2 each A4 sheet can need up to 4 code pages.

1. Shared constant (pdf.ts). Define `CODE_MIN_CELL = 2.2` and use it in both drawSheet and StepPdf so the PDF and the UI cannot disagree.

2. Code-sheet pages (pdf.ts).
- Add a `variant: 'lay' | 'codes'` parameter to drawSheet.
- In the sheet loop (pdf.ts:517-525), after each 1:1 ('lay') sheet whose cells are too small for codes, compute k = ceil(CODE_MIN_CELL / min(tileW,tileH)/s) with a minimum of 2. Do not limit k to {2,3,4}.
- Split exactly the same cell range [c0,c1)×[r0,r1) with the existing split() logic at scale s·k. Call drawSheet(..., 'codes') for each part.
- Code pages keep the same row/column labels, stone colours and codes.
- Title: 'Codeplan zu Blatt A1-1 (Teil j/m) – NICHT maßstäblich (k:1) – nicht zum Auflegen'.
- Code pages leave out the registration crosses, join lines, markHint and calibration bar. Without the calibration bar they also fall outside the existing test filter.
- Add a light diagonal border or watermark so a code page cannot be mistaken for a laying sheet.
- On the section cover, list the 'lay' sheets only and note '+ m Codeplan-Seiten'.

3. Find the cell on the 1:1 sheet. Text inside 0–1 mm joints does not fit, so instead:
- Draw 0.1 mm guide lines every 10 cells on the joint centre lines, as in cross-stitch charts.
- Repeat the row and column labels on the right and bottom edges.
- Draw the same 10-cell lines on the code pages.

4. Small cut pieces at any scale (pdf.ts:592). If a sheet otherwise shows codes but has pieces under 1.8 mm, do not make a whole code page. Print a short footer list 'Kleinteile ohne Nummer: ID → Farbcode' using the real IDs from cellId. Limit it to the sheet, with a '+n weitere' overflow.

5. UI (StepPdf.tsx).
- Fix tooSmallCodes for fit mode by computing the real per-section scale as pdf.ts:454 does.
- Add a checkbox 'Codeplan-Seiten beilegen (nicht maßstäblich)' that is switched on automatically when codes are hidden. Add the extra pages to the sheet estimate (the existing >300 warning stays).
- Rewrite pdfui.codesTooSmall in de, en and tr. Suggested German: 'Steine zu klein für Nummern auf 1:1-Blättern – Codeplan-Seiten (vergrößert, gleiche Zeilen/Spalten) werden beigelegt.' Add any new keys to all three languages; tests/i18n.test.ts checks that de, en and tr have the same keys.

6. Tests (tests/pdf.test.ts).
- Put a marker on code pages (for example the text 'Codeplan') and leave those pages out of the per-colour fill count, so the 1:1 count still equals stats.pieces.
- Add a test with 2×2 mm tiles at 1:1 that checks:
  - the code pages contain exactly one code per piece in the covered range;
  - the codes counted per colour equal stats.perColor;
  - the 1:1 sheets are unchanged (same fills and the same registration-cross positions).

Cheap first step, effort S, can ship before the M work: fix the fit-mode warning, and change the warning text to say that a 1:1 export for laying plus a 2:1 export as a code reference works today, because the row and column labels are the same.

findings.title: PDF step hides that the default PDF has 138 pages (98 of them coordinate lists); single-section printing is not reachable from the sections

1) One shared page planner, no drift: add `planPdfPages(layout, sections, opts, piecesPerSection, templateGroupCount?)` in src/core/pdf.ts (or pdfPlan.ts). 2) Show the breakdown in StepPdf before generation, e.g. 'ca. 138 Seiten: Deckblatt, 2 Bilder, Übersicht, Legende, 2 Material, 4 Abschnittsblätter + 16 Verlegeblätter, 13 Schnittvorlagen, 98 Koordinatenseiten'. 3) Make the default print file lean but complete for laying. Set DEFAULT_PDF_OPTIONS.includeCoords = false and keep the toggle. Fix the global coordLimit truncation (pdf.ts:817-829): apply the limit per section, or, if it would cut a selected section, warn in the UI before generating ('Koordinaten für A3, A4 fehlen – Abschnitte einzeln exportieren') instead of silently leaving them out.

4) Build the 'Inhalt' list from the options: grey out and strike through 'Originalfoto/Vorschau', 'Schnittvorlagen' and 'Koordinaten' when they are off, and show each item's page count from the planner.

Add 'PDF {sec.id}' next to 'CSV {sec.id}' (StepPlan.tsx:226) that calls it with an option override `{ sectionIds: [sec.id] }`. Do not write the override into rec.pdfOptions. globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
